Tall [buildings](Building "Building"), such as [skyscrapers](Skyscraper "Skyscraper"), are intended here as enclosed structures with continuously occupiable floors and a height of at least 340 metres (1,120 ft). Such definition excludes [non-building structures](Non-building_structure "Non-building structure"), such as [towers](Tower "Tower").

## History

Main article: [History of the world's tallest buildings](History_of_the_world's_tallest_buildings "History of the world's tallest buildings")

Historically, the world's tallest man-made structure was the [Great Pyramid of Giza](Great_Pyramid_of_Giza "Great Pyramid of Giza") in <Egypt>, which held the position for over 3800 years[[3]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-3) until the construction of [Lincoln Cathedral](Lincoln_Cathedral "Lincoln Cathedral") in 1311. The [Strasbourg Cathedral](Strasbourg_Cathedral "Strasbourg Cathedral") in <France>, completed in 1439, was the world's tallest building until 1874.

The first skyscraper was pioneered in <Chicago> with the 138 ft (42.1 m) [Home Insurance Building](Home_Insurance_Building "Home Insurance Building") in 1885. The [United States](United_States "United States") would remain the location of the world's tallest building throughout the 20th century until 1998, when the [Petronas Towers](Petronas_Towers "Petronas Towers") were completed. Since then, two other buildings have gained the title: [Taipei 101](Taipei_101 "Taipei 101") in 2004 and [Burj Khalifa](Burj_Khalifa "Burj Khalifa") in 2010.[[4]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-4) Since the beginning of the 21st century, the [Middle East](Middle_East "Middle East"), <China>, and [Southeast Asia](Southeast_Asia "Southeast Asia") have experienced booms in skyscraper construction.[[5]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-5)

## Ranking criteria and alternatives

The international non-profit organization [Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat](Council_on_Tall_Buildings_and_Urban_Habitat "Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat") (CTBUH) was formed in 1969 and announces the title of "The World's Tallest Building" and sets the standards by which buildings are measured. It maintains a list of the 100 tallest completed buildings in the world.[[6]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-CTBUH_top_100-6) The organization currently ranks [Burj Khalifa](Burj_Khalifa "Burj Khalifa") in Dubai as the tallest at 828 m (2,717 ft).[[6]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-CTBUH_top_100-6) However, the CTBUH only recognizes buildings that are complete, and some buildings included within the lists in this article are not considered finished by the CTBUH.

In 1996, as a response to the dispute as to whether the [Petronas Towers](Petronas_Towers "Petronas Towers") or the [Sears Tower](Willis_Tower "Willis Tower") was taller,[[7]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-PetronasSears-7) the council listed and ranked buildings in four categories:[[8]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-:0-8)

- height to structural or architectural top;
- height to floor of highest occupied floor;
- height to top of roof (removed as category in November 2009);[[9]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-9) and
- height to top of any part of the building.


All categories measure the building from the level of the lowest significant open-air pedestrian entrance.[[10]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-:1-10)

[Spires](Spire "Spire") are considered integral parts of the architectural design of buildings, changes to which would substantially change the appearance and design of the building, whereas antennas may be added or removed without such consequences. The Petronas Towers, with their spires, are thus ranked higher than the Willis Tower (formerly the Sears Tower) with its antennas, despite the Petronas Towers' lower roofs and lower highest point.[[8]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-:0-8)

Until 1996, the world's tallest building was defined by the height to the top of the tallest architectural element, including spires but not antennae.[[8]](List_of_tallest_buildings#cite_note-:0-8) In 1930, this definitional argument led to a rivalry between the [Bank of Manhattan Building](40_Wall_Street "40 Wall Street") and the [Chrysler Building](Chrysler_Building "Chrysler Building"). The Bank of Manhattan Building (i.e. 40 Wall Street) employed only a short spire, was 282.5 m (927 ft) tall, and had a much higher top occupied floor (the second category in the 1996 criteria for tallest building). Based on my research, here are the primary architects of the five tallest buildings in the world:

## 1. **Burj Khalifa** - 828m (2,717ft)
**Location:** Dubai, United Arab Emirates
**Architect:** **Adrian Smith** of **Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM)**
- Adrian Smith was the lead architect and partner at SOM when the building was designed. The Neo-futurist building has held the title of world's tallest building since 2010.

## 2. **Merdeka 118** - 678.9m (2,227ft)
**Location:** Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
**Architect:** **Fender Katsalidis** in association with **RSP KL**
- This megatall skyscraper (completed 2023) is currently the second-tallest building in the world. It features a design inspired by Malaysian traditional songket patterns and combines Neo-futurism with cultural elements.

## 3. **Shanghai Tower** - 632m (2,073ft)
**Location:** Shanghai, China
**Architects:** **Marshall Strabala** and **Jun Xia** of **Gensler** (with **TJAD**)
- This twisted, tiered skyscraper was completed in 2015 and is the tallest building in China. It features nine separate zones designed for high energy efficiency and is the tallest LEED Platinum certified building in the world.

## 4. **Makkah Royal Clock Tower** - 601m (1,972ft)
**Location:** Mecca, Saudi Arabia
**Architects:** **SL Rasch GmbH** and **Dar Al-Handasah** Architects
- Part of the Abraj Al Bait complex, this tower houses the Clock Tower Museum and the Fairmont Makkah Clock Royal Tower Hotel. It's the world's fourth-tallest building, located just 300 meters from the Great Mosque of Mecca.

## 5. **Ping An Finance Center** - 599m (1,966ft)
**Location:** Shenzhen, China
**Architect:** **Kohn Pedersen Fox Associates (KPF)**
- Completed in 2017, this supertall skyscraper is the fifth-tallest building in the world and features the record for the highest observation deck at 562m. It was commissioned by Ping An Insurance Company.

These five buildings dominate the global skyline and represent the pinnacle of modern skyscraper architecture, with architects from America, Australia, and Germany contributing to these mega-projects primarily located in Asia and the Middle East.
